quizName: DMV Practice Test #2 20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: Low-speed crashes:

options.text: Happen frequently, so there is no need to worry about them.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen at speeds below 30 miles per hour. Even crashes at low speeds can be fatal.

questions.question: For the best protection, riding gloves should be made of:
questions.explanation: Gloves should be made of leather or another strong, durable material to protect your hands.

questions.question: If drinking alcohol, you should:

options.text: Decide if you are still fit to ride based on how you feel after you finish drinking.
Set a limit beforehand so you can still safely ride.
Not be concerned about your riding abilities if you feel fine.

questions.explanation: The safest choice is to not ride after drinking any alcohol. Even small amounts of alcohol can affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: Which of the following does not need to be checked regularly?
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tires, controls, chains, sprockets, shock absorbers, fasteners, and brakes. Small mechanical problems can be very dangerous on a motorcycle.

questions.question: When operating a motorcycle on a slippery surface, you should:
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down. Use both brakes when stopping and avoid sudden movements.

questions.question: ____ can remove alcohol and its effects from your body.
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. Coffee, exercise, fresh air, and cold showers cannot reduce alcohol's effects. They may keep you awake, but they do not lower your blood alcohol level or make you sober.

questions.question: Can clothing help prevent injuries in a crash?

options.text: No, clothing is not really for protection.
No, clothing is more of a personal choice.
Yes, but only if garments are very loose and flap in the wind.
Yes, if pants and a jacket cover your arms and legs completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, if pants and a jacket cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Proper clothing reduces injuries in a crash. Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs, are made of sturdy material, and fit snugly so they don't flap in the wind.

questions.question: Which of the following should you inspect during a pre-ride check?

options.text: The general wear and tread of your tires
The amount of cushion your seat has

questions.correctAnswerText: The general wear and tread of your tires
questions.explanation: Before every ride, do a full check of your motorcycle. Inspect your tires, oil and fluid levels, headlight, tail light, turn signals, brake light, clutch and throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: Mirror checks:

options.text: Should be part of your normal scanning routine.
Should be avoided because they will distract you.
Should be avoided since other drivers will see you easily.
Are only recommended in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be part of your normal scanning routine.
questions.explanation: Know what is behind you for safety. Check your mirrors often as part of your regular scanning routine.

questions.question: Keep extra space between your motorcycle and the vehicle in front of you:

options.text: When conditions will make stopping more difficult than usual.
When you want to look at the scenery.
To encourage other drivers to cut you off.
To prevent the driver in front of you from knowing you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: When conditions will make stopping more difficult than usual.
questions.explanation: Keep more distance if it will take longer to stop. Increase your following distance on slippery roads, when you cannot see ahead, or in heavy traffic where cars may try to cut in front of you.

questions.question: Most crashes happen in daylight. To be more visible, you should:
questions.explanation: Since most crashes happen in daylight, wear bright-colored clothing while riding. This helps other drivers see you.

questions.question: When riding, goggles:

options.text: Protect your eyes, but not your whole face.
Protect your face, but not your eyes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect your eyes, but not your whole face.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes. A face shield protects your whole face. Eyeglasses are not enough protection for either.

questions.question: When checking your motorcycle before riding, make sure:

options.text: The brakes make a loud squeaking noise.
The brakes cause friction with the steering.
Each brake can hold the motorcycle.
Only the rear brake can hold the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each brake can hold the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Test each brake lever before every ride. Both brakes should feel firm and hold the motorcycle when fully applied.

questions.question: If you borrow a motorcycle:

options.text: Expect it to handle like your own bike.
The owner will check the brakes for you.
Leave extra space between you and other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave extra space between you and other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Check a borrowed motorcycle the same way you check your own. Ride carefully and leave extra space to stop. An unfamiliar bike may handle differently.

questions.question: A motorcycle has the best traction on which surface?
questions.explanation: Dry pavement gives the best grip. Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lines, and metal plates are all slippery and dangerous.

questions.question: A motorcycle fits you properly if:

options.text: You can touch the ground with your feet while seated.
You can reach the controls by stretching.
The handlebars go over your head.
Your feet cannot reach the foot pegs.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can touch the ground with your feet while seated.
questions.explanation: A good fit means your feet reach the ground when you sit on the bike. You should easily reach and operate all controls.

questions.question: When checking tires before riding, you should look at everything except:
questions.explanation: Check air pressure, tread, and wear on your tires before each ride. Shininess does not affect tire safety.

questions.question: What helps reduce head and neck injuries in a crash?
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the most important thing you can do to protect your head and neck during a crash.

questions.question: Which type of clothing helps other drivers see you?
questions.explanation: Wear bright, reflective clothing to help other drivers see you and your motorcycle on the road.

questions.question: Riding at night is usually:

options.text: Easier than the day because you can see other vehicle lights.
Harder than the day because visibility is worse.

questions.correctAnswerText: Harder than the day because visibility is worse.
questions.explanation: Night riding is more challenging because it is harder to see and be seen. Shadows and light contrasts are missing, which makes it hard to judge distances.
